issues.description: Ruff UP007/UP035/UP045 disabled wholesale with a TODO instead of completing the Union -> | migration the PR advertises.
issues.detail: The PR description promises PEP 604 unions, but ruff.toml ignores exactly the rules that would enforce it, leaving the codebase in a two-dialect state indefinitely. Either land the auto-fix as a follow-up patch in this series or scope the ignore to specific paths with a tracking link. A blanket repo-wide ignore is the wrong shape for a migration.

issues.description: default_raise shim and stale <3.10 comments left behind after kw_only_dataclass removal.
issues.detail: default_raise is documented as a <3.10 compatibility workaround, and the comment above TransactionEndpointRequest still references that rationale. With kw_only=True universally available, required fields can use native dataclass semantics instead of a RuntimeError sentinel. Either remove the shim and use real required-field semantics, or update the comments to state the actual current invariant.

issues.description: Install-script CI prep hardcodes python3.12 and includes a debug `dnf search` line.
issues.detail: The Amazon/Rocky prep steps now force python3.12 specifically instead of letting the test matrix (3.10/3.11/3.12) drive the version, so those distros silently test only one interpreter. The added `dnf search python3.12` is debug noise that adds nothing to the install postcondition and can mask real failures. Drop the search and pin to the matrix minimum.

issues.description: install.sh version guard still allows Python 3.7-3.9 while printing a ">= 3.10" error.
issues.detail: The guard reads `PYTHON_MINOR_VER -lt 7` but the error message claims 3.10+ is required. A 3.8 interpreter passes the check with a contradictory message. Bump the literal to 10 so code matches string.

issues.description: itertools.pairwise refactor in test_priority_mutex.py is unrelated to 3.9 removal and not applied broadly.
issues.detail: Replacing zip(ordered, ordered[1:]) with itertools.pairwise is a fine 3.10 win but is a separate logical change from dropping 3.9. Either split it into its own patch or grep the rest of the tree and apply the idiom uniformly so the codebase carries one shape for the same operation.

synthesis.summary: The Python 3.9 removal is mechanically clean and correctly shaped where it actually deletes the version forks (cmd_classes.py is the template). But the patch is half-done in three places the panel agrees on: ruff disables exactly the UP rules that would enforce the new PEP 604 union style the PR advertises, the default_raise sentinel and <3.10 comments survive as dead scaffolding in wallet_request_types.py, and CI install steps both hardcode python3.12 (breaking matrix coverage) and carry a debug `dnf search` line. Finish the ruff conversion (or land it as the next patch), strip the stale compatibility shims, and tighten the install.sh guard and CI prep before this is done.
